name: Beauty Pill
label: Dischord
lede: Beauty Pill started as a Dischord band the Dischord crowd didn't quite know what to do with, then lived through Chad Clark's failing heart, an album recorded in a museum and a transplant without ever settling into one shape.

eras.title: What came after Smart Went Crazy
eras.text: Smart Went Crazy had won over DC's post-hardcore crowd with Con Art in 1997. When it came apart, its singer, a studio obsessive named Chad Clark, started what Dischord's bio calls a shape-shifting musical project, with his vision and constant change as its only fixed parts.

years.h: Smart Went Crazy ends, and Chad Clark starts Beauty Pill
years.p: [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] and Abram Goodrich bring in Joanne Gholl to make an EP, and the project has a name.

years.h: The Cigarette Girl from the Future is Dischord No. 128.5
years.p: Beauty Pill's first EP comes out on Dischord and DeSoto Records together. The same year, Clark masters [[El Guapo|be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd]]'s Super/System for Dischord.

eras.title: The wrong room
eras.text: With Rachel Burke's voice out front, Beauty Pill made records that sound, now, like a band a few years ahead of its audience. Dischord's crowd wanted the old post-hardcore, and Clark would later tie the whole era to the feeling of failing.

years.h: Rachel Burke takes the mic and Beauty Pill becomes five
years.p: [[Rachel Burke|1fd466ef-ace6-4e44-bf53-aa0ef692908e]] joins on vocals, with Basla Andolsun on bass, Drew Doucette on guitar and [[Ryan Nelson|758a01ba-b700-4b52-809a-917da0bb30e5]] on drums.

years.h: You Are Right to Be Afraid is Dischord No. 138
years.p: The second EP is the second of Beauty Pill's three Dischord releases in four years.

years.h: The Unsustainable Lifestyle is the last Dischord record
years.p: Dischord No. 139 is Beauty Pill's first full-length. The Washington City Paper covered its return two decades later, on the Blue Period anthology.

years.big: Sometimes the last people to understand your new band are the people who liked your old band
years.h: A Pitchfork review leaves Chad Clark feeling like a failure
years.p: Clark told Rolling Stone a Pitchfork review of the time felt negative, and he still ties Beauty Pill's Dischord records to the feeling of failing. The line above is Ian MacKaye's advice, as Clark tells it.
years.xp:
Clark's own explanation for the cold reception: "Beauty Pill had a distinct femininity in the way that we sounded and approached what we were doing."

He says [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] told him the line about old and new audiences when the band's sound shifted. Clark took it as a mismatch, not a verdict.

years.cap: Beauty Pill live at Modern Formations, Pittsburgh, July 2006
years.h: Rachel Burke heads to Seattle, and Jean Cook takes the vocals
years.p: [[Jean Cook|c304c9c2-e3f3-4abb-b7ca-61f86f4889f5]] takes over vocals and strings. Drummer Ryan Nelson leaves to form [[Soccer Team|16cf8c3c-93a7-40a4-be20-460491346d49]], and [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]] replaces him.

eras.title: A virus in the heart
eras.text: Just as the new line-up settled, Clark nearly died. He kept the diagnosis private, survived emergency surgery, and spent two years recovering out of sight, writing the whole time and building a reading-and-music series on the side.

years.h: Chad Clark goes into emergency open-heart surgery
years.p: A virus had been inflaming Clark's heart since fall 2007 (viral cardiomyopathy), and he told almost no one. Emergency open-heart surgery in February 2008 made it public.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls the condition rare. Clark told Rolling Stone he got "an electronic heart in early 2008": a battery-powered device that kept blood moving. "If you put your head against my chest, you would hear this whirring sound and not a heartbeat."

The surgery worked. Clark spent the next two years recovering privately, and writing, while Beauty Pill went quiet.

years.h: Recovering, Chad Clark builds a stage for writers
years.p: Clark curates and hosts Story/Stereo, a series pairing writers and musicians at DC's Writer's Center. It goes on to win National Endowment for the Arts funding.

eras.title: Recording in public
eras.text: The comeback happened in a museum. Arlington's Artisphere commissioned Beauty Pill to make an album in public, and the record that came out of it in 2015 landed on critics' year-end lists.

years.cap: Clark, Cook, Doucette, Andolsun and Ocampo on the spring 2015 tour, April 30
years.h: Eleven years after its last album, Beauty Pill releases a double LP
years.p: Beauty Pill Describes Things as They Are is the band's first album away from Dischord. It was recorded in public in 2011, as a residency at Artisphere in Arlington, Virginia.
years.xp:
The residency, Immersive Ideal, turned the making of the album into an exhibit people could walk into. Wikipedia's album page says they finished a song a day. The line-up was the one Clark had since 2005: Jean Cook, Devin Ocampo, Abram Goodrich, Basla Andolsun and Drew Doucette.

It made NPR's 50 best albums of 2015 and Rolling Stone's best albums you didn't hear. Magnet named it album of the year, Robert Christgau ranked it seventh, and Time later called it one of the ten best albums of the decade. Pitchfork, whose earlier review had stung, gave it a 7.5.

eras.title: A borrowed heart
eras.text: Beauty Pill became an art-space band, touring museums with Arto Lindsay and finally releasing a play score it had made in 2010. Then the device that had kept Clark alive was recalled, and he needed a transplant.

years.cap: Beauty Pill at the Luce Foundation Center, Smithsonian American Art Museum, May 20, 2016
years.h: Beauty Pill tours art spaces with Arto Lindsay
years.p: One of Chad Clark's heroes, [[Arto Lindsay|6c1904f2-dacf-4389-b828-d2cedc6f12b4]], is the tour partner for 2016 and 2017, and the dates are mostly museums.

years.cap: Beauty Pill at AIGA DC's Punk Rock Type event, September 14, 2018
years.h: Jean Cook leaves, and Erin Nelson sings
years.p: [[Erin Nelson|e770cef7-21c3-487c-a211-d2050fe6a9a7]] replaces Jean Cook, who had sung and played strings with Beauty Pill since 2005.

years.cap: Beauty Pill at Seventh Stanine Festival, Rhizome DC, June 15, 2019
years.h: A play score waits ten years, then becomes Sorry You're Here
years.p: Beauty Pill scored suicide.chat.room, a play directed by Marcus Kyd, in 2010. The score comes out in 2020 alongside a new EP, Please Advise.
years.xp: Paulina Guerrero choreographed the play. The A.V. Club called the score "brilliant and vividly balletic"; the Washington Post, "smartly evocative."

years.h: Instant Night goes out on a 12" single
years.p: Beauty Pill's 12" single Instant Night comes out in December.

years.cap: Beauty Pill with Laurie Anderson's Kludge, Joe's Pub, New York, October 16, 2021
q: I'm borrowing [this heart] from some beautiful soul.
years.h: Chad Clark waits weeks for a heart that fits
years.p: The maker recalls his heart device, and Clark is hospitalized in spring 2022. A donor heart has to suit a man six foot four, and Rolling Stone reports the transplant came that summer.
years.xp: Clark told Rolling Stone he is "extremely, profoundly grateful" for another person's heart, and that everything he does for the rest of his life will be a risk. "And the band is worth it."

years.h: Beauty Pill Describes Things as They Are returns for Record Store Day
years.p: The 2015 album recorded in public at Artisphere gets a Record Store Day reissue.

years.h: Blue Period collects the Dischord years, demos included
years.p: The double-album anthology on Ernest Jenning gathers The Unsustainable Lifestyle, You Are Right to Be Afraid, outtakes and demos. Clark had resisted revisiting the era for years.
